key_insight: Geo-FSRL selects stochastic transitions that minimize update-induced conditional KL divergence within a coefficient-preserving Gaussian policy family for few-step flow reinforcement learning.
engineering_relevance: It improves reinforcement-learning fine-tuning on the original few-step schedule while retaining the deterministic solver at inference.
method: Reduce policy selection to a scalar geometry factor governing conditional KL, velocity-space Fisher information, and log-likelihood-ratio variance.
Derive a unique closed-form optimum using both source and target noise levels, shared across all nonzero velocity updates.
Apply gradient-scale matching with closed-form policy-gradient and KL weights to normalize timestep-dependent scales.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports higher final reward scores than Flow-GRPO and Flow-CPS on both image and video generation models in the 4-step setting, without numerical results.
watch_item: The optimality guarantee is restricted to the specified coefficient-preserving isotropic Gaussian family; broader policy families and step counts require validation.
paper_title: Optimizing Stochastic Policy Geometry for Few-Step Flow Reinforcement Learning
